title: Updates for the family
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in general surgery. Mr Rowe, 70, is recovering from bowel surgery and has capacity. His three adult children phone the ward several times a day, each asking for detailed updates.

Mr Rowe hasn't said what he wants shared with them.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Tell callers he is comfortable, until you have spoken to him.
options.brief: Gives minimal information while you check.
options.detailed: Saying very little until you know his wishes is cautious. It ranks third.

options.text: Refuse to speak to the family at all.
options.detailed: This may upset them unnecessarily before you know what he wants.

options.text: Suggest, with his agreement, that the family chooses one contact for updates.
options.detailed: A single point of contact makes updates clearer for everyone. It ranks second because it depends on his wishes.

options.text: Give each of them full updates, as they are his children.
options.detailed: Being his children doesn't entitle them to his information. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Ask Mr Rowe what he'd like shared, and with whom.
options.detailed: He has capacity, and the decision about sharing his information is his. Asking him resolves the uncertainty. It ranks first.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you make sure a capacitous patient decides what his family is told.
explanation.keyDetails: He has capacity. He hasn't said what he wants shared. His family calls often.
explanation.reasoning: [E] asks him, [C] simplifies communication with his agreement, and [A] is cautious in the meantime. [B] is unhelpful, and [D] breaches confidentiality.
explanation.competing: [A] might be seen as a disclosure. Saying that someone is comfortable, without detail, is usually acceptable while you check.

references.title: Confidentiality: good practice in handling patient information
references.note: Sharing information with relatives with the patient's agreement.
